title: Se in Formal Writing: The Agreement Rule

sections.content: You know passive *se* and impersonal *se* from B1 Unit 6, and the cases with a person from B2 Unit 19. Formal writing (reports, notices, corrections) uses them constantly and applies the norm strictly. If a thing follows *se*, it is the subject, so the verb agrees with it in number. If *a* and a person follow, the person is an object, there is no subject to agree with, and the verb stays singular. Speech often breaks both rules (*se vende casas*, *se entrevistaron a los autores*), and an editor marks them.

sections.title: One rule, four sentences
rows: The report was published. (singular thing: singular verb)
The data were published. (plural thing: plural verb)
An author was consulted. (a + person: singular verb)
The authors were consulted. (a + people: still singular)

items.spanish: Se corrigieron las erratas del primer capítulo.
items.english: The misprints in the first chapter were corrected.

items.spanish: Se entrevistó a los autores del manual.
items.english: The authors of the manual were interviewed.

items.spanish: Se informó a todas las lectoras.

sections.content: Ask what follows *se*. A thing: copy its number (*se cambió la norma*, *se cambiaron las normas*). *A* and people: always singular (*se informó a los lectores*). *Se vende casas* is common on signs, but formal text has *se venden casas*, and a plural verb with *a* (*se informaron a los lectores*) is just as wrong.
